title: In one MICrONS mouse, synapses of one connection share a size component only for layer 2/3 and layer 4 excitatory axons, and the component does not follow co-tuning
abstract: We tested whether synapses of the same connection share a size component beyond cell and location effects, and whether this component follows functional similarity. We used cleft sizes of 13.7 million synapses between typed cells in the MICrONS minnie65 volume (release v1300), and the 2,042 cells with proofread axons. A double-difference estimator compared each within-connection synapse pair with distance-matched same-axon, same-target and unrelated controls. It removes axon, target and smooth spatial terms. On synthetic data it recovered a true value of 0.30 as 0.31. For excitatory-to-excitatory connections, the connection-specific component was 0.16 to 0.22 of size variance (35,424 multi-synapse connections). For excitatory-to-basket, excitatory-to-Martinotti, and basket or Martinotti outputs, it was near zero (-0.03 to 0.04). It depended on the presynaptic type: 0.32 (0.27 to 0.36) for layer 2/3 axons, 0.20 for layer 4 axons, and below 0.07 for layer 5 and layer 6 axons, onto all target types. It did not decrease from 20 to more than 80 um between synapses. Co-tuned pairs had larger mean synapses (slope 0.58 SD per unit signal correlation after cell fixed effects), but signal correlation explained about 2% of the component. The component did not change with signal correlation (slope 0.008, -0.035 to 0.051, per SD; 3,815 connections). A two-state mixture did not isolate the shared part. Limitations: one mouse, cleft size as a strength proxy, no spine or shaft labels, selected proofread axons, and noisy functional measures. Code, aggregate results, figures, source hashes and a retrieval script are included.
